terms.grammar: impersonal of appāreō, with an accusative and infinitive or a question
evidence: Ter. Eun. 485: appāret servum hunc esse dominī pauperis
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: appāret states what is plain to see; vidētur, what seems so to the speaker (see seem). For “appear, come into sight” see appear.
From scīre licet, “one may know”; often ironic (Lewis & Short; see of course).

evidence: Cic. Fin. 2.75: rem vidēlicet difficilem et obscūram!
terms.comment: From vidēre licet, “one may see”; classical, but much rarer than scīlicet, and ironic too (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.342: perspicuum est igitur alia esse in homine optanda, alia laudanda

terms.comment: Traupman gives it for “obviously” (p. 353); classically it is “palpably”, said above all of someone caught in the act (Plaut., Cic.: Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: nōn dissimulat, patrēs cōnscrīptī: appāret esse commōtum; sūdat, pallet.
phrases.english: He does not hide it, senators: he is obviously upset; he is sweating, he is pale.

phrases.latin: Appāret servum hunc esse dominī pauperis
phrases.english: Obviously this slave belongs to a poor master

phrases.latin: ā tē litterās exspectābam, nōndum scīlicet; nam hās māne rescrībēbam.
phrases.english: I was expecting a letter from you — not yet, obviously, for I am writing this in the morning.
